findings.title: Outcome timing is conflated in the Lepper reward example
findings.source_location: Section5 p4 closing sentence of Overjustification Effect paragraph
findings.suspect_step: Uses a quality measure taken during experimental sessions as if it supported decline after reward removal
findings.complete_check: Primary Lepper methods p133 and results p135 locate drawing quality during experimental sessions; p134 measures later free-choice time, 7-14 days after sessions
findings.alternative_reading: 'These findings suggest' can signal extrapolation; under that reading later quality effect is untested, not disproven
findings.impact: Local evidence-scope mismatch; no demonstrated falsification of motivational mechanism or central design recommendation
findings.dependency: Illustrative support in Section5; no estimated post-removal performance effect enters subsequent conclusions

repair.statement: Separate immediate drawing quality from subsequent voluntary engagement; mark later-performance effect as extrapolation

unresolved_claims.claim: Full causal chain from reward design to crowding-out to LLM usage and long-term data quality
unresolved_claims.status: Proposed mechanism; not newly validated in this paper

counterevidence: Explicit support for compensation and beneficial incentives
Explicit acceptance of judicious AI assistance
